Definition: {a house (in the greatest variation of applications, especially family, etc.)}
BiblicalUsage: Bayith is the Aramaic word for house, and it is the word for the house of God in the days of exile and return. Daniel goes to his house and tells his companions to seek mercies of the God of heaven, Daniel kneels in his house with his windows open toward Jerusalem, Zerubbabel and Jeshua rise up and build the house of God at Jerusalem, and Cyrus commands that the house be built in its place.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the house in exile is the promise that God has not moved out, because Daniel prays toward a house that lies in ruins and the exiles come home to rebuild it. The house of God is the place where His people meet Him, and I hold that the God who answers Daniel in his house still answers His people in His house today.
